title: Pullback preserves bounded constructibility
statement:
Let $\Lambda=P_n$ be as in
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-direct-image-finiteness] and let $g:V'\to V$ be
a morphism of schemes. The derived pullback $Lg^*=g^{-1}$ restricts to an
exact triangulated functor
$$
 Lg^*:\Dbc(V_{\Proet},\Lambda)\longrightarrow\Dbc(V'_{\Proet},\Lambda),
$$
and carries the class of objects with cohomology in $[a,b]$ into the same
class.

note:
*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this form. Stacks' nearest
entries are the equivalence defined by $\epsilon^{-1}$ between constructible
sheaves on $X_{\Et}$ and on $X_{\Proet}$, Lemma 61.27.2 ([Tag
09AK](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09AK)), its complex-level form
for bounded below complexes, Lemma 61.27.4 ([Tag
09AL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09AL)), and the weak Serre
property of the constructible category, Lemma 61.27.3 ([Tag
09B5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09B5)); the constructibility
entries Definition 61.29.1 ([Tag
09C1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C1)) and Proposition 61.29.7
([Tag 09C7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C7)) are stated for a
Noetherian scheme and a Noetherian coefficient ring and concern adic
constructibility, and no entry states that a pullback preserves a
cohomological interval. Difference: the blueprint adds the exactness of
$Lg^*=g^{-1}$ on the finite coefficient rings $P_n$ and the preservation of
the interval $[a,b]$, for the bounded constructible categories of
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-direct-image-finiteness].

proof.text: Choose $K\in\Dbc(V_{\Proet},\Lambda)$. By the definition of this subcategory, choose $L\in\Dbc(V_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $K\cong\nu_V^*L$. On etale module sheaves, inverse image acts on the underlying abelian sheaf, with the pulled-back constant coefficient action. Kernels and cokernels are those of the underlying abelian sheaves, so the exactness proposition implies exactness on these modules. For a complex $C$, put $Z^i=\ker d^i$ and $B^i=\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}=\ker(\operatorname{coker}d^{i-1})$. Exactness identifies the pulled-back cycles and boundaries with $g^{-1}Z^i$ and $g^{-1}B^i$; taking their quotient gives $\mathcal H^i(g^{-1}C)\cong g^{-1}\mathcal H^i(C)$. The exact-functor factorization represents the derived etale pullback by this termwise complex.

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence; definitions of bounded constructibility

proof.text: Apply the constructible etale abelian-sheaf pullback lemma to the underlying abelian sheaf of each $\mathcal H^i(L)$. It gives a finite constructible stratification on $V'$ with finite locally constant underlying set sheaves. These restrictions are also finite locally constant as $\Lambda$-modules: on an etale neighbourhood trivializing the finite set $M$, refine around any geometric point so that the values of addition on every pair in $M$, zero, negation on $M$, and scalar multiplication for every $(r,m)\in\Lambda\times M$ are constant. This requires only finitely many refinements because $\Lambda$ and $M$ are finite. The fixed tables satisfy the module identities because the original operations do, giving a constant finite $\Lambda$-module on that neighbourhood. Thus each $g_{\Et}^{-1}\mathcal H^i(L)$ is constructible as a module sheaf. By step 1 these are the cohomology sheaves of $g_{\Et}^{-1}L$, and the bounded-constructible criterion applies.

source.place: ## Proof, partition description of a constructible complex

proof.text:
For a complex $C$ representing $L$, apply the comparison isomorphism in each degree: $
u_{V'}^*g_{\Et}^{-1}C^r\cong g_{\Proet}^{-1}
u_V^*C^r$. Naturality for $d^r:C^r	o C^{r+1}$ says the component isomorphisms commute with the differentials, so they form an isomorphism of complexes. The comparison acts on fixed finite-coefficient module sheaves, and the pro-etale operations and comparison inverse image are exact and applied termwise. Hence this yields $Lg^*K\cong
u_{V'}^*(g_{\Et}^{-1}L)$ in the derived category. Step 2 and the essential-image definition of $\Dbc(V'_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ now put $Lg^*K$ in this subcategory; no complex-level comparison equivalence is assumed.

The pro-etale module inverse image is exact by the pro-etale operations definition. The cycles, boundaries, and quotient calculation of step 1, now applied directly to any representative of $K$, gives $\mathcal H^i(Lg^*K)\cong g_{\Proet}^{-1}\mathcal H^i(K)$. Thus if $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$, these same degrees vanish after pullback, since an additive functor sends zero to zero. The operations definition already supplies a triangulated functor on the ambient derived categories. Its shifts and distinguished triangles restrict to the bounded-constructible full subcategories preserved in step 3, giving the asserted exact triangulated restriction. To justify the subcategory structure used here, the etale bounded-constructible category is triangulated by [prop-constructible-derived-subcategory]. The exact comparison is fully faithful on bounded-below complexes by [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. Given a map between two pro-etale objects with bounded-constructible etale witnesses, full faithfulness lifts it to a map between those witnesses. Its etale cone is bounded constructible; the triangulated comparison sends this cone triangle to a cone triangle for the original map, so its cone has etale origin. Shifts and zero have etale witnesses by applying comparison to the etale shift and zero. Thus the essential-image full subcategory is triangulated.

split_report.summary: Four-step proof using the etale origin in the definition of pro-etale bounded constructibility, exact termwise inverse image, finite-coefficient module constructibility, and degreewise natural comparison. No new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Proof paragraph: etale exactness and partition argument (steps 1-2), then the sheaf comparison applied degreewise (step 3); interval preservation directly on pro-etale cohomology (step 4).

tool_uses.why: The step uses its general theorem that inverse image of a constructible finite-stalk etale abelian sheaf remains constructible; this generic tool lemma is from the constructibility unit and is not restated in the proper-base-change route.
Generic finite-coefficient etale bounded-constructible triangulated-subcategory result needed to justify the essential-image subcategory; the proper-base-change unit has no separate closure lemma.
